decisions.detail:
The National VET Regulator has cancelled, under s 56 of the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011, all VET qualifications issued by Arizona College Pty Ltd, also trading as Invention Academy, RTO 1412 between 24 January 2024 and 14 June 2025.

Note: There were multiple effective dates for this regulatory action. The dates shown above reflect the last decision made. The first effective date was 12 August 2025.

This decision affects the following qualifications:

Qualifications

• CHC33015 Certificate III in Individual Support

• CHC40313 Certificate IV in Child, Youth and Family Intervention

• CHC43015 Certificate IV in Ageing Support

• CHC43115 Certificate IV in Disability

• CHC43315 Certificate IV in Mental Health

• CHC50413 Diploma of Youth Work

• CHC52015 Diploma of Community Services

• CHC53315 Diploma of Mental Health

• CHC62015 Advanced Diploma of Community Sector Management

Further information about this regulatory action is available on ASQA’s website: www.asqa.gov.au

Potentially impacted individuals who are not sure if their qualifications or statements of attainment have been cancelled can contact ASQA for verification. Details on how to do this are available from www.asqa.gov.au/about/contact-us.

decisions.detail:
The National VET Regulator has cancelled, under s 56 of the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011, some VET qualifications and statements of attainment issued by Gills College Australia Pty Ltd (RTO 2417) (trading as Elite College Australia and/or Sterling Business College) between 7 January 2022 and 21 December 2023.

Note: There were multiple decision and effective dates for this regulatory action. The dates shown above reflect the last decision made. The first decision was made on 13 December 2024, with an effective date of 20 December 2024.

This decision affects the qualifications and statements of attainment listed below. ASQA cancelled these qualifications and statements of attainment where it identified specific concerns, however some qualifications and statements of attainment listed below were not cancelled and continue to be valid.

Qualifications

• AUR30620 Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology

• AUR40216 Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis

• CHC30121 Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care

• CHC33015 Certificate III in Individual Support

• CHC43015 Certificate IV in Ageing Support

• CHC43115 Certificate IV in Disability

• CHC43315 Certificate IV in Mental Health

• CHC50121 Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care

• CHC51015 Diploma of Counselling

• CHC52015 Diploma of Community Services

• CHC53315 Diploma of Mental Health

Units of competency on statements of attainment

• HLTAID009 Provide cardiopulmonary resuscitation

• HLTAID011 Provide First Aid

• HLTAID012 Provide First Aid in an education and care setting

Exceptions

As noted above, ASQA has cancelled only the qualifications and statements of attainment for which it identified specific concerns. Not all qualifications or statements of attainment listed above, or issued by Gills College Australia (trading as Elite College Australia and Sterling Business College), have been cancelled.

Further information about this regulatory action is available on ASQA’s website: www.asqa.gov.au

Potentially impacted individuals who are not sure if their qualifications or statements of attainment have been cancelled can contact ASQA for verification. Details on how to do this are available from www.asqa.gov.au/about/contact-us.

decisions.decision: Impose condition(s) on the provider's registration
decisions.detail:
The RTO must for the period of its current registration, retain and provide to ASQA within fourteen (14) days upon request:

• copies of student files, for a period of 18 months from the date which a final judgement of competence is made for all VET courses delivered, the including copies of all:

• marked assessment records (including any document which informed a determination of competence)

• master assessment tools

• learner and trainer guides

• training and assessment strategies

• pre-enrolment forms (including any document which informed whether the student’s English language proficiency, educational qualifications, or work experience is sufficient to enable a learner to enrol in a course)

• evidence of student intervention and support in accordance with student support policy

• student progress results across all units in all courses.

The RTO must for the period of its current registration, retain and provide to ASQA within fourteen (14) days upon request:

• evidence of implementation of internal review/remediation action as follows:

• quarterly internal audit report and associated changes

• remediation actions after 13 December 2019 (e.g. completed gap assessments, supplementary classes)

• timetables for all classes, at all locations, for all students, for each training period, which must include for each unit of competency:

• course code and title

• location and classroom

• designated trainer(s)

• first name and surname of allocated students

• dates of training and any term breaks

• scheduled class start and end times, including class breaks.

• attendance monitoring records (i.e. utilising new biometric system, and hardcopy signed records where appropriate)

• attendance policy and procedure.

The RTO must review its assessment system against clause 1.8 of the Standards, and conduct validation and moderation of select training products on its scope of registration, being:

• AHC40316 Certificate IV in Production Horticulture,

• AHC50316 Diploma of Horticulture, SIT40516 - Certificate IV in Commercial Cookery,

• and any new training package product that would be automatically added to the scope of registration because it is equivalent to one which appears above; by 30 September 2020, and in accordance with the requirements with clauses 1.9 and 1.11 of the Standards. The moderation must sample a minimum of 10 completed student files for each selected training product on its scope of registration. A report must be produced of the moderation findings for each student file, including primary evidence of any gap training or reassessment conducted, refunds provided, qualifications cancelled, and evidence of the outcome of any recommendations made as a result of the moderation activity. These reports must be retained by the applicant, and made available to ASQA on request, for the period of its current registration with effect 35 calendar days after the date the RTO is given written notice of the decision.

Impose, under s 29(1) of the NVR Act, the following conditions on the RTO’s registration:

• for the entire period of its current registration, Executive Security Training Pty Ltd, must securely retain, and provide to ASQA on request, copies of all completed student assessment items for each student (per the definition in ASQA’s General Direction – Retention requirements for completed student assessment items and clearly identifiable as to which student and unit/s each item relates to)

• for the entire period of its current registration, Executive Security Training Pty Ltd, must securely retain, and provide to ASQA on request copies of the master assessment tools used for each assessment, for a period of 18 months from the date on which the judgement of competence for each relevant unit of competency is made

• executive Security Training Pty Ltd, must notify ASQA, in writing, at least one month before commencing delivery of nationally recognised training or conducting assessment for each training product that it is approved to deliver. This condition is not a regulatory sanction against the organisation.

with immediate effect.

STAY DECISION CONDITIONS 23 JULY 2026

- The Applicant is permitted to enrol, train and assess a limited number of students (not to exceed 30 students per calendar month in aggregate) across the following four training products:

(a) HLTAID011 Provide First Aid.

(b) HLTAID009 Provide Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.

(c) HLTAID012 Provide First Aid in an education and care setting.

(d) CPC WHS 1001 Prepare to work safely in the construction industry.

- The Applicant is to complete the training and assessment of any student enrolled for a training course referred to in Order 3 in a given month by the last business day in that calendar month and to provide the Respondent with a copy of its file for each student enrolled, trained and assessed in a calendar month as soon as reasonably practicable after the end of that calendar month.

- The Applicant is to continue the engagement of the services of RTO Advance for the purpose of RTO Advance providing oversight of the training and assessment of students by the Applicant under the terms of these Orders and shall inform the Respondent promptly should the Applicant’s engagement of RTO Advance cease for any reason.

- The Applicant is to provide the Respondent with a copy of the contract of engagement for each trainer who will be providing training and assessment of students (prior to any training being provided by that trainer) under the terms of these Orders.

- The Applicant must inform all prospective students and third-party contractors of the Respondent’s cancellation of registration decision referred to in Order 2, of this proceeding, and that the Applicant is only enrolling new students pending the determination of this proceeding in accordance with the terms of these Orders.

- The Applicant is to inform the Tribunal and the Respondent within 7 days of becoming aware of any material change of circumstances which affects its ability to comply with these Orders.

decisions.decision: Impose condition(s) on the provider's registration
decisions.detail:
Every 6 months for a period of 18 months from the date of decision, the applicant is to provide to ASQA evidence of:

• all Compliance Management Committee meetings held, including, but not limited to:

• meeting minutes and agendas,

• records of any issues identified by the committee and the steps taken to address and monitor the rectification of those issues.

• an up-to-date continuous improvement register, or any other document the applicant uses to:

• identify systemic or other compliance issues,

• record the steps to be taken to rectify those issues, and

• monitor the implementation and effectiveness of those steps

• all steps taken to systematically review and monitor the accuracy of data entered into PRISMS and ensure compliance with the ESOS Act in reporting relevant data in PRISMS.

• any compliance and/or quality assurance reviews of the applicant’s systems, processes and procedures completed by the applicant’s external compliance consultants.

• the steps the applicant has taken to continue to monitor and review the implementation of the new and revised systems and policies it has adopted to rectify the non-compliance identified by ASQA’s Compliance team.

• any steps the applicant has taken to strengthen its regulatory compliance and governance processes.

Note: Through the conditions imposed on the applicant’s NVR registration, if non-compliance is identified in any of the evidence submitted by the applicant, ASQA will immediately commence a regulatory activity comprising a comprehensive review of the applicant’s compliance with its obligations under the NVR and ESOS Acts.

assessment records for all VET students for all VET courses for a period of two

the date of this decision for the period of its registration maintain a record of the

following in relation to the assessment:

• the location;

• the nature, time and duration of the activity;

• the student ID of the student where relevant;

• the identity of the trainer/assessor conducting the training or

assessment activity; and

• a detailed description of the activity and any outcome.

student ratio the Applicant must, commencing from the date of this decision for

the period of its registration, maintain a complete attendance record that

includes:

• whether the person attended in their capacity as a student or as an

acting customer for each relevant activity; and

• where the person attended as an acting customer, the first and last

name of that individual, their signature and email address.

checklists for each unit of competency to be provided to the Respondent on

request.

decisions.detail: The AAT has pursuant to section 41(2) of the Administrative Appeals Tribunal Act 1975, the Tribunal, that the implementation of the decisions under review is stayed subject to the conditions that: a) the RTO must not enrol any new students; b) the RTO must retain and continue to retain all student pre-enrolment, enrolment and training and assessment records for all students; c) from 30 November 2018 (date of stay order) for a period of six months, and in accordance with 8.1, and 8.10 of the National Code of Practice for Providers of Education and Training to Overseas Students 2018 (National Code), the RTO must implement and maintain minimum attendance requirements for overseas students as a condition of its registration; and, must keep, maintain and produce those records on request to ASQA; d) the RTO, must maintain and produce on request to ASQA, class rolls for each class, containing the name of each student scheduled to attend that class, signed by each student who did attend that class at the commencement and ceasing of each class and signed by each trainer/assessor training or assessing in that class, for all VET courses; e) the RTO, for the purposes of clause 8.13 of the National Code, must assess whether a student has maintained satisfactory course attendance at the end of each week in the study period; f) for the purposes of clause 8.12 of the National Code, the RTO's process for determining the point at which an overseas student has failed to meet satisfactory course attendance must be at the point that the student has failed to attend any greater amount than 20% of the total of the scheduled contact hours for the course in a study period; g) for the purposes of clause 8.12.3 of the National Code, the RTO's policy and process for monitoring and recording attendance of the overseas students require the RTO to identify, notify and assist students who have been absent for 5 consecutive days of the scheduled course contact hours, even where those days are not adjacent to one another; h) from 30 November 2018 at the end of each month for the prior month, the RTO must produce to ASQA to [email removed] marked attention to The Proper Officer, a spreadsheet with the following information: i. for a period of three months, for the entire student cohort a spreadsheet containing: 1. on the spreadsheet obtained from the RTO's student management system in an excel format, listing each student with their first name, last name and student ID, and; 2. spreadsheet information obtained from the RTO's student management system in an Excel format including; student number, student last name, student first name, date of birth, course name, current attendance percentage, overall attendance percentage, consecutive days absent, absences in period (the month) and total hours in period (the month); and ii. date each month: 1. providing ASQA with a spreadsheet produced from the RTO's student management system in an Excel format as described in (i)2. above; 2. identifying if each student has been issued a warning letter, a breach of attendance letter or has been reported for non-attendance and the date on which such a letter is issued. i) upon the RTO addressing the identified non-compliances on which the decisions were based to the satisfaction of ASQA and upon the notification of same by ASQA to the Tribunal, orders 2 a) - h) will cease to have effect.

decisions.decision: Impose condition(s) on the provider's registration
decisions.detail:
The following conditions are imposed on the Applicant’s registration under section 29(1) of the NVR Act until 23 May 2028, with the Applicant to keep written records of such conditions having been complied with, and such records to be kept updated and produced to ASQA (at [email removed]) upon request and within the specified timeframe:

Student Monitoring and Enrolment

3.2.1 The Applicant must retain and present to ASQA on request pre-enrolment, enrolment, support and progression or training assessment records, for all VET students for all VET courses for the duration of its registration, with such records to be retained for a period of two years following the student completing or last undertaking studies with the Applicant and for the duration of the new registration period, whichever is latest.

3.2.2 The Applicant must not at any time have more than 600 studying students in total in qualifications on its scope of registration during the current registration period.

3.2.3 The Applicant must maintain records of student attendance for all classes. This includes signed class rolls that record student arrival and departure times, reasons for early departures, and student and trainer/assessor signatures. The Applicant must implement procedures to monitor attendance patterns and intervene where necessary to support student progression. Attendance records must be retained for the duration of the student’s enrolment and be available to ASQA upon request.

3.2.4 Upon a request by ASQA for a copy of records referred to in the Student Monitoring Condition above, the Applicant must

provide to ASQA the relevant records within five business days of the request.

decisions.decision: Impose condition(s) on the provider's registration
decisions.detail:
The following conditions are imposed on the Applicant’s registration under section 29(1) of the NVR Act until 23 May 2028, with the Applicant to keep written records of such conditions having been complied with, and such records to be kept updated and produced to ASQA (at [email removed]) upon request and within the specified timeframe:

3.1 Condition 1: Compliance Reviews

3.1.1 The Applicant must engage an external consultant to monitor its compliance with the Standards for RTOs and the ESOS framework, including governance, assessment, student support, and record keeping on an ongoing basis. The external consultant will prepare an annual compliance report based on the findings of the monitoring process and any improvements which the Applicant has made.

3.1.2 The Applicant will prepare an action plan in response to each compliance report, to address any identified issues or opportunities for improvement. Each compliance report and the resulting action plans shall be tabled at management meetings.

3.1.3 All compliance reports, action plans, and supporting documentation will be retained for the duration of the Applicant’s registration.

3.1.4 The Applicant must implement a documented system to monitor the quality and consistency of assessment practices across all training products on its scope. This system must include scheduled internal reviews of a sample of assessment tools and outcomes, verification of assessor qualifications and competencies, and mechanisms to ensure assessments are conducted in accordance with training package requirements. Records of these reviews and any corrective actions taken must be retained.

3.1.5 The Applicant must establish and implement a documented system to regularly review and verify that all training and assessment facilities are appropriate and sufficient to support the delivery of each training product on its scope of registration. This system must ensure that facilities are fit for purpose, to industry standards, meet the requirements of the relevant training packages, and are adequate to accommodate the number of enrolled students. Reviews must be conducted at least annually, or prior to any increase in student numbers or changes to delivery arrangements. Records of facility assessments, including identified gaps and corrective actions, must be retained.

3.1.6 Upon a request by ASQA for a copy of any records referred to in this Condition, the Applicant must provide to ASQA the relevant records within five business days of the request.

decisions.detail:
Scope and Capacity

The total capacities of the applicant at its locations will be a cumulative total of 350 current students at any given time across the following locations combined:

a. Unit 3C Level 3 40 Raymond Street, BANKSTOWN, New South Wales 2200

b. Level 7, 95-99 York Street SYDNEY NSW 2000

• The applicant will not apply to add to scope of courses during the registration period other than adding to scope a course which becomes superseded in which case the new replacement course shall not count as an addition to scope but rather a replacement or amendment to scope.

• The applicant will not apply to change capacity during the registration period.

• Bi-Annual Compliance Reviews

• The applicant will engage an external, independent consultant to conduct compliance reviews in each June and November within the registration period from the date of the terms of consent decision signed by the parties.

• Following each review, a compliance report will be prepared, and the CEO and/or RTO Manager will develop an action plan to address any identified issues or opportunities for improvement.

• Action plans and evidence of corrective actions will be tabled at management meetings and monitored until all non-compliances or issues are resolved.

• All compliance reports, action plans, and supporting documentation will be retainedfor the duration of the registration period and presented to ASQA on request.

• Student Monitoring and Enrolment 5

• The applicant must retain and present to ASQA on request pre-enrolment, enrolment,

• support and progression or training assessment records, for all VET students for all VET courses for a period of two (2) years from the date on which the student ceases to be a student.

• The applicant must maintain class rolls for each class that the registered provider conducts as part of any VET course offered by the applicant, with the roll to:

a. contain the name of all students who are scheduled to attend that class;

b. be signed by each student who is present at the commencement of the class, or, if a student arrives late to the class, on their arrival at the class;

c. be signed by each student who is present at the end of each class, or if a student leaves class early, include why they leave the class early; and

d. be signed by each trainer or assessor who provided the training or assessment in that class.

decisions.detail:
Condition 1 -

NPA will engage an external independent consultant

with appropriate expertise and experience to provide advice, by 28

February 2026:

A. addressing the systemic implementation of policies and

procedures that is evidence based

B. addresses whether timetabling procedures being

implemented by NPA ensures that the maximum number of

students scheduled to be in the facilities at any one time is

not exceeding the maximum capacity imposed by Condition

5, including in circumstances where there is another tertiary

education provider scheduled to use the facility at the same

time as NPA

C. identifying the impact of any non-compliance areas and

remedial action to address the identified impacts of current

and past non-compliance

D. identifying what further actions, if any, NPA should take to

strengthen its compliance with the National Vocational

Education and Training Regulator (Outcome Standards for

Registered Training Organisations) Instrument 2025 (2025

RTO Standards) and the National Code of Practice for

Providers of Education and Training to Overseas Students

2018 (National Code);

ii. NPA will provide ASQA (at [email removed]) with a copy of

the report and recommendations produced by the expert within 14

days of it being finalised;

iii. NPA will ensure that action plans and evidence of corrective and

remedial actions are tabled at management meetings and are

monitored until any non-compliances identified by the external

independent consultant referred to in (i) above are resolved;

iv. For the period of registration, NPA will ensure that all compliance

reports, action plans and supporting documentation (including

management meeting records) are retained and made available to

ASQA on written request within 14 days of the written request.

decisions.decision: Impose condition(s) on the provider's registration
decisions.detail:
1. Within the first 3 months of its registration, the Applicant must not do any of the following:

• enrol any students;

• deliver any training to students; and

• issue any VET qualifications or statements of attainment

2. Within the first 3 months of its registration, the Applicant is to provide to the Respondent a document detailing the proposed structure and governance arrangements for the RTO (registered training organisation). This document must:

• include details of the role, functions and responsibilities of the CEO, board of directors, and, if applicable, the RTO’s dedicated compliance officer; and

• explain how each of these individuals/bodies will interact with the sole owner and director of the company, who is to have no involvement in the day-to-day operations or management of the RTO.

3. The Respondent will have the right to veto the appointment of any new CEO or dedicated compliance officer (if any) identified by the Applicant if the Respondent does not consider the person to be a Fit and Proper Person in accordance with the requirements in Schedule 3 of the Standards for NVR Registered Training Organisations 2015 (Cth) (Standards for RTOs). Prior to the commencement of the proposed new CEO or dedicated compliance officer, the Applicant must ensure the person completes and submits a Fit and Proper Person declaration to the Respondent. The Respondent must notify the Applicant as soon as practicable, or at the latest, within 28 days, as to whether it considers the proposed person to be a Fit and Proper Person. If the Respondent is satisfied the person is a Fit and Proper Person, the Applicant may then appoint them.

Impose, under s 29(1) of the NVR Act, the following condition on the provider's registration, consistent with its renewed registration period of 01 November 2028:


The provider must for the period of registration provide the VET Regulator, commencing on 31 October 2024, a report annually detailing:


• how it is ensuring it is sufficiently resourced for all products on scope at all times, including copies of any documents created, used or relied upon to determine this; and


• validation activities undertaken, including reports and evidence of implementation of any recommendations arising from those activities; and


• how the RTO ensures its operations are quality assured as required by Clause 2.1 of the Standards for RTOs, including by detailing, its systems and processes and the implementation of those systems and processes to ensure it complies with each clause of the Standards for RTOs at all times; and


• the progress of any compliance monitoring or quality assurance activity it has undertaken in relation to ensuring compliance with each clause of the Standards for RTOs in the preceding reporting period and that it has scheduled in the following 12 months; and,


• copies of any documents created, used or relied upon to monitor and/or ensure compliance and quality as referred to in that description.

The AAT has pursuant to section 41(2) of the Administrative Appeals Tribunal Act 1975, the Tribunal, that the implementation of the decisions under review is stayed subject to the conditions that: a) the RTO must not enrol any new students; b) the RTO must retain and continue to retain all student pre-enrolment, enrolment and training and assessment records for all students; c) from 30 November 2018 (date of stay order) for a period of six months, and in accordance with 8.1, and 8.10 of the National Code of Practice for Providers of Education and Training to Overseas Students 2018 (National Code), the RTO must implement and maintain minimum attendance requirements for overseas students as a condition of its registration; and, must keep, maintain and produce those records on request to ASQA; d) the RTO, must maintain and produce on request to ASQA, class rolls for each class, containing the name of each student scheduled to attend that class, signed by each student who did attend that class at the commencement and ceasing of each class and signed by each trainer/assessor training or assessing in that class, for all VET courses; e) the RTO, for the purposes of clause 8.13 of the National Code, must assess whether a student has maintained satisfactory course attendance at the end of each week in the study period; f) for the purposes of clause 8.12 of the National Code, the RTO's process for determining the point at which an overseas student has failed to meet satisfactory course attendance must be at the point that the student has failed to attend any greater amount than 20% of the total of the scheduled contact hours for the course in a study period; g) for the purposes of clause 8.12.3 of the National Code, the RTO's policy and process for monitoring and recording attendance of the overseas students require the RTO to identify, notify and assist students who have been absent for 5 consecutive days of the scheduled course contact hours, even where those days are not adjacent to one another; h) from 30 November 2018 at the end of each month for the prior month, the RTO must produce to ASQA to [email removed] marked attention to The Proper Officer, a spreadsheet with the following information: i. for a period of three months, for the entire student cohort a spreadsheet containing: 1. on the spreadsheet obtained from the RTO's student management system in an excel format, listing each student with their first name, last name and student ID, and; 2. spreadsheet information obtained from the RTO's student management system in an Excel format including; student number, student last name, student first name, date of birth, course name, current attendance percentage, overall attendance percentage, consecutive days absent, absences in period (the month) and total hours in period (the month); and ii. date each month: 1. providing ASQA with a spreadsheet produced from the RTO's student management system in an Excel format as described in (i)2. above; 2. identifying if each student has been issued a warning letter, a breach of attendance letter or has been reported for non-attendance and the date on which such a letter is issued. i) upon the RTO addressing the identified non-compliances on which the decisions were based to the satisfaction of ASQA and upon the notification of same by ASQA to the Tribunal, orders 2 a) - h) will cease to have effect.

6.     The applicant must provide documented evidence demonstrating that all trainers and assessors hold current and valid qualifications and vocational competencies as required Outcome Standard 3 (Clauses 3.2 and 3.3) of the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Outcome Standards for NVR Registered Training Organisations) Instrument 2025 (Outcome Standards)  and Credential Policy Section 1A, and that the organisation has effective processes to ensure all its trainers and assessors meet, at all times, the mandatory qualification, vocational competency, and industry currency requirements as required in Outcome Standard 3.2 and 3.3

The following conditions are imposed on the Applicant’s registration under section 29(1) of the NVR Act until 23 May 2028, with the Applicant to keep written records of such conditions having been complied with, and such records to be kept updated and produced to ASQA (at [email removed]) upon request and within the specified timeframe:

Student Monitoring and Enrolment
3.2.1 The Applicant must retain and present to ASQA on request pre-enrolment, enrolment, support and progression or training assessment records, for all VET students for all VET courses for the duration of its registration, with such records to be retained for a period of two years following the student completing or last undertaking studies with the Applicant and for the duration of the new registration period, whichever is latest.
3.2.2 The Applicant must not at any time have more than 600 studying students in total in qualifications on its scope of registration during the current registration period.
3.2.3 The Applicant must maintain records of student attendance for all classes. This includes signed class rolls that record student arrival and departure times, reasons for early departures, and student and trainer/assessor signatures. The Applicant must implement procedures to monitor attendance patterns and intervene where necessary to support student progression. Attendance records must be retained for the duration of the student’s enrolment and be available to ASQA upon request.
3.2.4 Upon a request by ASQA for a copy of records referred to in the Student Monitoring Condition above, the Applicant must
provide to ASQA the relevant records within five business days of the request.

Impose condition(s) on the provider's registration

The following conditions are imposed on the Applicant’s registration under section 29(1) of the NVR Act until 23 May 2028, with the Applicant to keep written records of such conditions having been complied with, and such records to be kept updated and produced to ASQA (at [email removed]) upon request and within the specified timeframe:
3.1 Condition 1: Compliance Reviews
3.1.1 The Applicant must engage an external consultant to monitor its compliance with the Standards for RTOs and the ESOS framework, including governance, assessment, student support, and record keeping on an ongoing basis. The external consultant will prepare an annual compliance report based on the findings of the monitoring process and any improvements which the Applicant has made.
3.1.2 The Applicant will prepare an action plan in response to each compliance report, to address any identified issues or opportunities for improvement. Each compliance report and the resulting action plans shall be tabled at management meetings.

3.1.3 All compliance reports, action plans, and supporting documentation will be retained for the duration of the Applicant’s registration.
3.1.4 The Applicant must implement a documented system to monitor the quality and consistency of assessment practices across all training products on its scope. This system must include scheduled internal reviews of a sample of assessment tools and outcomes, verification of assessor qualifications and competencies, and mechanisms to ensure assessments are conducted in accordance with training package requirements. Records of these reviews and any corrective actions taken must be retained.
3.1.5 The Applicant must establish and implement a documented system to regularly review and verify that all training and assessment facilities are appropriate and sufficient to support the delivery of each training product on its scope of registration. This system must ensure that facilities are fit for purpose, to industry standards, meet the requirements of the relevant training packages, and are adequate to accommodate the number of enrolled students. Reviews must be conducted at least annually, or prior to any increase in student numbers or changes to delivery arrangements. The Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT) stayed ASQA’s decision to:a) cancel the Australian Institute of Professional Education Pty Ltd’s registration under section 39 of the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011 (Cth); andb) part cancel the Applicant’s registration under the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 (Cth) consisting of VET courses.Subject to the following conditions:a. the following statement is to appear on the Applicant’s website:Australian Institute of Professional Education Pty Ltd (AIPE) is a Registered Training Organisation within Australia that is subject to audit by Australia's national regulator, the Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA). AIPE is also registered to provide VET courses to overseas students.ASQA regulates courses and training providers to ensure nationally approved quality standards are met including providers who provide VET courses to overseas students. Where standards are not met ASQA may decide to cancel the training provider's registration. This means the training provider will not be able to continue teaching any courses.ASQA believes that AIPE does not meet certain standards and has taken the decision to cancel AIPE’s registration as a VET training provider, including its registration to deliver VET courses to overseas students.AIPE believes it does meet all relevant standards and has challenged the decisions by ASQA to cancel its registration.The challenge is currently before the Administrative Appeals Tribunal, being a body that provides independent review of administrative decisions by ASQA.AIPE anticipates that the outcome of the Tribunal's review will be known within the next 4 to 6 months.AIPE is entitled to continue to provide courses pending the Tribunal's decision.See further: http://www.asqa.gov.au/about-asqa/regulatoty-decisions/asqa-decisions.htmlb. the above statement will be provided in writing to:i. all students applying for and offered enrolment in VET qualifications from 25 January 2016;ii. all international students who have purchased a package of courses which includes a VET qualification and are currently studying at AIPE; andiii. all other international students who have purchased a package of courses which includes a VET qualification at the time they commence their studies with AIPE.
